name: JORDAN

flag.title: Flag of Jordan
flag.note: Black, white & green with red chevron

lead: Jordan is a desert kingdom in the Middle East where a city was carved from rose-red rock, a sea so salty you float without swimming, and Bedouin tribespeople have roamed vast sandy landscapes for centuries. It sits at a crossroads where Africa, Asia, and Europe once traded spices and silk.
geo: Jordan is mostly golden desert and rocky plateau, split by the Great Rift Valley. The Dead Sea — the lowest place on Earth at around 430 m below sea level — shimmers with water so salty nothing can live in it. The Jordan River snakes along the western edge.

In the south, Wadi Rum glows orange at sunset. Its towering sandstone pillars look so alien that film-makers use it as a stand-in for Mars. The north has green hills and olive groves, and Aqaba gives Jordan its only slice of coastline.
animals: The Arabian oryx — a white antelope with long straight horns — was hunted to extinction in the wild, but a global rescue programme bred it back and herds were released into Wadi Rum in 2009. The sand cat, a tiny golden wildcat with huge ears, hunts lizards by night and never needs to drink water.

Griffon vultures soar on warm air above the Dana Biosphere Reserve. The Azraq wetland oasis — the only freshwater marsh for hundreds of kilometres — is a vital pit-stop for millions of migrating birds every spring and autumn.
culture: Jordanians are famously hospitable. Refusing cardamom-spiced coffee is rude; tiny cups keep coming until you tilt yours sideways to say 'enough'. The national dish, mansaf, is lamb slow-cooked in dried-yoghurt sauce over fragrant rice, eaten by hand around a communal tray.

Friday is the day of rest and families gather for long lunches after prayers. Amman's Roman amphitheatre still hosts concerts. Traditional embroidery — bright red cross-stitch on black cloth — is worn at festivals and sold in every market.
history: The Nabataeans carved an entire city — Petra — into rose-red cliffs about 2,000 years ago, growing rich controlling spice and silk routes. Rome absorbed their kingdom; the colonnaded city of Jerash, one of the best-preserved Roman towns outside Italy, still stands near Amman.

Crusaders built castles, Saladin reclaimed the land, and the Ottomans ruled for 400 years. After World War I Jordan became a kingdom. King Abdullah II, in power since 1999, traces his lineage to the Prophet Muhammad — 41 generations back.
wows: The Dead Sea is about 10 times saltier than the ocean — you float without any effort.
Petra was unknown to outsiders for centuries; a Swiss explorer disguised himself to sneak in in 1812.
Wadi Rum doubled as Mars in the film 'The Martian' — its red sand looks extraterrestrial.
Amman is built on seven hills, just like Rome — locals call them 'the Seven Jebels'.
The Jordan River shrinks to barely 30 metres wide after so much water is diverted upstream.
Jordan is one of the world's most water-scarce countries — second-driest on Earth by some counts.
Azraq Wetland dried up by 1992 but conservationists refilled it; migrating birds returned fast.

myths.fact: The north has lush green highlands with oak forests and apple orchards — Ajloun gets up to 500 mm of rain a year and feels nothing like a desert.

myths.myth: The Dead Sea is almost gone
myths.fact: Its level drops about 1 metre per year, which is serious — but that still leaves a very long time before it disappears, and conservation work continues.
